correctness.rationale: The four-unit antipodal-pair lemma follows from e1=e3=0 for unit complex roots. Each matching yields either one frequency or a complete line by a determinant equal to (ti-tj)(tk-tl)(ti+tj-tk-tl). No three matchings can be feasible for odd p. In a feasible parallel matching, normalized sine decomposition excludes all off-line roots by equal moduli and u!=±v. Zero, one, two and line witnesses establish exact ranges. A pure integer/cyclotomic checker passed 104626 checks including complete discrete-phase enumeration for p=5,7. Finite checks supplement, not prove, the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Fixed-support phase-only uncertainty across p+1 MUBs is a natural exact harmonic-analysis invariant. The sharp flat bound p improves the unrestricted p+2 at exactly four sites, and the support geometry causes a growing p-versus-2 zero-count transition. It classifies every attainable zero count and every line maximizer for all odd primes, useful for support-constrained MUB diagnostics and phase-only Fourier design. No downstream or noise theorem is claimed.
